messages:
Ivy L: opened a tiny docs PR to add a canary checklist for Dedicated provisioning + a short SDK + YAML example. PR: https://git.redwood/docs/pull/980
Marco H: quick note: canary runbook should explain isolation decorators vs tenant_labels, and a short rollback step.
Samira P: agree. proposed YAML canary snippet:
```yaml
reservation:
  name: canary-search
  gpus: 1
  tenant_labels:
    - team:search
  isolation_decorators:
    - soft-isolate
scalePolicy:
  mode: target_utilization
  target_utilization: 0.5
  cooldown_sec: 60
  preemption_behavior: graceful
```
DevRel Sam: small Python SDK snippet for canary creation (users can paste):
```python
from redwood import DedicatedClient
c = DedicatedClient()
res = c.create_reservation("canary-search", gpus=1, tenant_labels=["team:search"], isolation_decorators=["soft-isolate"])
res.update_scale_policy(target_utilization=0.5, cooldown_sec=60, preemption_behavior="graceful")
```
ops-oncall: ops notes: "graceful" gives up to 60s drain; for true non-preemptible workloads use `hard_isolate` and reserved capacity SLA applies. Canary rollback: set scalePolicy target_utilization=0 and deprovision after 2m. Also mention quota enforcement window (15m).
legal: SLA text: please avoid "best effort". propose: "Reserved capacity SLA: 99.95% monthly availability for active reservations. Preemption only for emergency or critical maintenance; scheduled maintenance will include 24h notice."
Ivy L: will update PR with YAML + SDK + canary rollback steps + legal phrasing and ping ops for runbook link. Anyone object?
Marco H: no objections. small nit: use snake_case in YAML fields.
Samira P: I'll also add a one-line migration note: legacy `cooldown` -> `cooldown_sec`.
Ivy L: thanks all  aiming to push edits today and request legal review. :thumbsup:
